title.narrative: NIHR Reducing delays in cancer care in sub-Saharan Africa

description.narrative: A UK and low-middle-income country partnership (University of Ibadan, Bayero University, African Population and Health Research Center, Kenya Medical Research Institute, University of Birmingham, University of Edinburgh, University of Warwick, University of Exeter, Georgetown University) that aims to develop and then evaluate a service change to avoid delay in receiving cancer care. This study will take place over 54 months from November 2024 - April 2029. Cancer is the second largest cause of death in Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) and the outlook for cancer is much worse in SSA than in high-income countries, mostly because people already have late-stage, and therefore incurable, disease by the time they are diagnosed. Approximately half of the delay arises after the person has been to a clinic: it is this delay within the health sector that we will study.

We will build on our ongoing relationships with local governments in two countries: Oyo and Kano states in Nigeria, and Nairobi County in Kenya. These countries are increasingly using public messaging to encourage people with serious symptoms to attend health clinics, and they are upgrading specialist services. It is therefore crucial to close the gap and provide an effective, efficient, compassionate, and equitable pathway from presentation at a primary health clinic to receiving specialist treatment. We will study care for people with symptoms of seven ‘marker’ cancers; uterus (womb), colon, breast, stomach and gullet (oesophageal), lung, prostate/bladder/kidney, and head/neck. Working with patients, policymakers and civil society we will design interventions to reduce delay arising in primary health clinics by designing an educational programme and to reduce delays after referral by developing a programme of peer navigation assistance.
To evaluate clinician education we will test knowledge through structured tests and then measure the knowledge practice gap based on observations. We will evaluate both interventions by monitoring referral rates, patient wellbeing and delay. To better understand factors that influence successes of our interventions, we will study the broader system, including workforce, collaboration between organisations, leadership and governance.
Community members and policymakers will work with us to disseminate findings and engage people across SSA and beyond so that they can learn from what we have done and advocate for similar services locally.

participating-org.narrative: Health Research Operations Kenya Limited - The Operating Vehicle for the KEMRI-Wellcome Trust Research Programme

recipient-country.narrative: African Population Health Research Center (APHRC) will lead delivery of research activities in Kenya. APHRC, inter-agency non communicable diseases technical working group Kenya Ministry of Health, Kenya National Control Programmes and Kenya Network of Cancer Organisations will also provide health systems support. Kenyatta National Hospital will provide advice and support on intervention development and pilot. Cancer Café will lead CEI activities across the collaboration along with support from other collaborators. at KEMRI-Wellcome Trust Research Programme Kenya will provide expertise in health economics and co-lead work package 6. Work packages 1-6 will take place in Kenya.

Collaborators from Georgetown University, University of California, San Francisco and Harvard University will lead work package 3 and provide expertise on quality measurement. Collaborators from University of California, San Francisco will support the continuation of literature review and curation for work package 6.

The University of Birmingham will provide overall leadership and management of the project with support of the University of Ibadan and it manages the overall programme of work and acts as the host contracting institution. University of Birmingham staff will provide expertise in priority setting, decision making in healthcare, intervention development and implementation studies. Collaborators will provide expertise in developing knowledge tests for medical education and medical schools assessment and to support work packages 2 and 5. The University of Birmingham will work with partners to lead on work package 5. The University of Warwick leads the qualitative research components across the programme. The University of Exeter provide advice across the whole research programme with primary support to work package 2 and the University of Edinburgh will provide scientific advice across the programme.

The University of Ibadan will provide overall leadership and management of the project with support of the University of Birmingham. The University of Ibadan will lead activities in Ibadan and will also provide expertise in intervention development, process evaluation, educational theory and research management. It will also lead training and capacity strengthening for the project. Bayero University will lead all activities in Kano and ensure input from the Federal Ministry of Health Nigeria. Bayero University will work with partners to lead on work packages 2, 4 and 5.
Work packages 2 - 6 will take place in Nigerian sites (Ibadan and Kano).
